description: GalaxyModel parameters (P4-A). Units: kpc, degrees, emissivity in Lsun(V) pc^-3, dust opacity kappa_V in 1/kpc. Model frame: origin Sgr A*, z = physical mid-plane normal (tilted so the Sun sits z0 above it), x from the Sun's projection towards the centre, y towards l = 90 deg (direction of rotation at the Sun). Arm azimuth beta (Reid 2019): 0 towards the Sun as seen from the centre, increasing in the direction of Galactic rotation (clockwise seen from the north Galactic pole).

sun.source: R0: GRAVITY Collaboration 2019, A&A 625, L10; z0: Bennett & Bovy 2019, MNRAS 482, 1417 (same values as src/core/units.ts)

thinDisk.source: hR, hz: Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard 2016, ARA&A 54, 529 (Table 6); j0 = 0.03 Lsun/pc^3 so that 2 j0 hz = 18 Lsun/pc^2, the local V-band disc surface brightness of Flynn et al. 2006 (MNRAS 372, 1149), approximate; inner depletion inside the bar (Freudenreich 1998, ApJ 492, 495, approximate)

thickDisk.source: hR 2.0 kpc, hz 0.9 kpc: Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard 2016, ARA&A 54, 529 (R_T = 2.0 +- 0.2 kpc, z_T = 900 +- 180 pc). norm = 0.12 is the thick/thin ratio of the mid-plane density at the Sun (it multiplies thinDisk.j0): the local density normalisation of Juric et al. 2008, ApJ 673, 864 (12%, fitted with scale heights of 300 and 900 pc), the highest of the published values (1% to 12%). It is not the estimate of Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard 2016: their local density ratio is f_rho = 4% +- 2%, and their 12% +- 4% is the surface density ratio f_Sigma = f_rho z_T / z_t. With 0.12 in the mid-plane the model's surface density ratio is 0.12 x 0.9 / 0.3 = 0.36, three times theirs. Kept as a model choice (docs/modules/milkyway.md, 'Model values against the cited papers'); approximate

bulge.source: Axis ratios of the boxy/peanut bulge from Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard 2016, ARA&A 54, 529 (section 4.2.1): y0/x0 = 0.5 is the axis ratio seen from the top, (b/a)_bp = 0.5 +- 0.05; z0/x0 = 0.26 is the edge-on axis ratio at the centre, (c/a)_bp = 0.26 (also the minor axis of the scale-length ratios 10:6.3:2.6 of Wegg & Gerhard 2013, MNRAS 435, 1874, which hold inside 1 kpc). The major axis lies along bar.angleDeg. Model choices, approximate: x0 = 1 kpc (scale of the Gaussian-type profile exp(-r_s^2 / 2) with r_s^4 = ((x/x0)^2 + (y/y0)^2)^2 + (z/z0)^4); one vertical axis ratio (the X shape is not modelled); j0 tuned so bulge + bar give ~1e10 Lsun(V)

bar.source: halfLength: long bar half-length 5.0 +- 0.2 kpc, near end at positive l (Wegg, Gerhard & Portail 2015, MNRAS 450, 4050). angleDeg = 27 is the bar angle of the boxy/peanut bulge to the Sun-centre line, 27 +- 2 deg (Wegg & Gerhard 2013, MNRAS 435, 1874; phi_bp in Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard 2016, ARA&A 54, 529), and orients both the bulge and the long bar. Wegg, Gerhard & Portail 2015 measure the long bar itself at 28 to 33 deg and find it consistent with being aligned with the bulge (one connected structure), so the model keeps one angle; the long bar is therefore drawn 1 to 6 deg below its measured range (model choice, approximate; docs/modules/milkyway.md, 'Model values against the cited papers'). Widths and j0 approximate

armProfile.source: Arm width grows 0.042 kpc per kpc of radius (Reid et al. 2019, ApJ 885, 131); stellar/optical arms drawn 2x the maser-traced widths (approximate); young-population emissivity, scale length/height and old-disk arm contrast (arm/interarm ~2, Drimmel & Spergel 2001, ApJ 556, 181) are approximate

dust.source: hR 5.0 kpc, hz 0.1 kpc (Misiriotis et al. 2006, A&A 459, 113); kappa_V tuned to ~1.3 mag/kpc in the local mid-plane and A_V ~30 mag towards Sgr A*; dust on the inner (concave) arm edges (density-wave shocks, Roberts 1969); R:V:B extinction ratios from Cardelli, Clayton & Mathis 1989 (R_V = 3.1); approximate

hii.source: Procedural HII clumps along the arms (one hashed clump per 0.5 kpc cell, ~45% occupied); colour of Halpha + Hbeta + [NII] emission; approximate, artist-level

warp.source: Chen et al. 2019, Nature Astronomy 3, 320 (classical Cepheids), power-law fit: height of the mid-plane z_w = a (R - R_w)^b sin(phi - phi_w) in kpc for R > R_w, with R_w = 7.72 kpc, a = 0.060, b = 1.33, phi_w = 17.5 deg; phi is the Galactocentric azimuth, 0 towards the Sun, increasing with Galactic rotation. Values checked against the fetched paper by tools/milkyway/features/structure.mjs. Model choice (blendKpc): the law is applied outside the solar circle only, blended in over 1 kpc, because the Sun's height z0 is measured from the local mid-plane, which stays the model plane

flare.source: Lopez-Corredoira & Molgo 2014, A&A 567, A106: scale height h_z(R) = h_z(Rsun) [1 + k1 (R - Rsun) + k2 (R - Rsun)^2] for the thin disc (k1 = -0.037 /kpc, k2 = 0.052 /kpc^2), and the same law in (R - R_ft) for the thick disc beyond R_ft = 6.9 kpc (k1 = 0.021, k2 = 0.006). Applied outwards of the Sun only and normalised so the scale heights at the Sun stay those of thinDisk and thickDisk (approximate). Values checked against the fetched paper by tools/milkyway/features/structure.mjs

photometry.source: Sun V-band-equivalent luminous flux 3.828e26 W x 93 lm/W (luminous efficacy of sunlight); calibration multiplier for continuity with the stars panorama (1 = none)
